role: National chair, Jonge Democraten (D66 youth organisation)
description: Chair of the D66-affiliated youth organisation, after chairing its Arnhem-Nijmegen branch (2007–2008). Parlement.com gives April 2008 to June 2009; the government CV gives 2008–2009.

role: Policy officer, D66 parliamentary group in the Senate
description: Policy staff member for the D66 senators. Parlement.com dates the post January 2008 – January 2009; the government CV gives 2007–2008.

role: Member and D66 group leader, Nijmegen municipal council
description: Elected at the head of the D66 list in 2010 and 2014; leader of the D66 group throughout, until he took his seat in the House of Representatives.
Management trainee from September 2011 and adviser from August/September 2013 at the state-owned rail infrastructure manager.

role: Regional construction manager, North-East Netherlands (based in Zwolle)
description: Regional manager for construction management (regiomanager Bouwmanagement) until his election to the House of Representatives.

role: Member of the House of Representatives (Tweede Kamer) for D66
description: Spokesman on economic affairs, climate and energy, gas extraction, rail and democratic renewal, later on medical ethics. Sponsored the second-reading constitutional bill on the appointment of mayors and King's commissioners and co-sponsored the Climate Act. Left parliament on becoming a minister.

role: Leader of the D66 parliamentary group in the House of Representatives
description: Succeeded Alexander Pechtold at 31, D66's youngest parliamentary leader. Parlement.com records two spells, 9 October 2018 – 8 March 2021 and 25 May – 28 September 2021, with Sigrid Kaag as party leader and lead candidate in 2021; Jetten had announced in June 2020 that he would not stand for the leadership.

role: Minister for Climate and Energy Policy (minister zonder portefeuille)
organization: Fourth Rutte cabinet (Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate Policy)
description: Responsible for climate policy, emissions trading, the Dutch Emissions Authority, energy policy and the Climate and Transition Fund. Steered the climate policy programme and the 2023 additional package for a 55% emissions cut by 2030, designated new offshore wind areas and Borssele as preferred site for two new nuclear plants, and in June 2022, during the gas crisis after Russia's invasion of Ukraine, lifted the 35% production cap on coal-fired power stations. Caretaker from July 2023 after the cabinet fell.
Succeeded Sigrid Kaag after she declined to lead D66 into the 2023 election; lead candidate in 2023 and 2025.

role: Member of the House of Representatives and leader of the D66 parliamentary group
description: Returned to the House after the November 2023 election while still a caretaker minister until 2 July 2024. Parlement.com dates his group leadership 23 November 2023 – 10 February 2026; the government CV gives 2 July 2024 – 23 February 2026 for the combined role. From 13 November 2025 to 10 February 2026 he chaired the House committee on the intelligence and security services (CIVD), a post that falls to group leaders.

role: Deputy Prime Minister (vice-minister-president); acting Minister of Finance
description: Took over the D66 posts of Sigrid Kaag after she left for a UN role on Gaza reconstruction. Parlement.com records him as Minister of Finance from 8 to 12 January 2024 (until Steven van Weyenberg's appointment) and as Deputy Prime Minister from 12 January to 2 July 2024.

organization: Tweede Kamer der Staten-Generaal (2025–2026 cabinet formation)
description: Appointed by a majority of the House after the debate on the D66–VVD–CDA coalition agreement 'Aan de slag' (30 January 2026); selected the ministers and state secretaries and delivered his final report on 21 February 2026.

role: Prime Minister (minister-president) and Minister of General Affairs
description: Heads a minority cabinet of 18 ministers (7 D66, 6 VVD, 5 CDA) and 10 state secretaries, with Dilan Yeşilgöz (VVD) and Bart van den Brink (CDA) as deputy prime ministers. The coalition holds 66 of 150 seats in the House and 22 of 75 in the Senate; the Parliamentary Documentation Centre describes it as the first minority cabinet since 1945.
